steps.content: Oliver... When I'm gone, you must listen to your aunt.
From now on, your aunt, uncle, and cousin will be your family...
You're a very sweet child, Oliver. You'll definitely get along with them, won't you...
It's all Mommy's fault... I've left you nothing...
During the trip back to the Bureau, Oliver resisted hard with all kinds of tricks and sweet talks. After being left in the confinement cell alone for a few days, Oliver finally begins to calm down.
Bleary-eyed, Oliver seems to have just woken up, but doesn't appear surprised to see you.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Hey, if it isn't Chief who's best at tricking Oliver?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oliver behaved so well while you were away! I didn't run away or cry! I'm a good child, aren't I?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: As a reward for my good behavior, can I go home now?
Oliver trots over enthusiastically, holding the toy and leaning toward you, looking just like a child longing for company.
But you've already seen the real Oliver in the factory and that house of mannequins.

options: Quit playing dumb. You can't fool me.

steps.content: You're too smart not to understand your current situation.
Your stern attitude seems to have genuinely taken Oliver aback. The kid returns to the seat forlornly.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Tsk... You were more fun as a doll and a sketchy rich person.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Now, you're no different from those stinky, annoying adults.
Oliver looks away and mutters into the toy. You can see the kid's knees shaking. After all, a place like this is too intimidating and stressful to a Sinner of Oliver's age.
Oliver... This is the MBCC, a Sinner supervision facility. We only carry out the interrogation to learn more about you. It won't take long.
Your tone softens slightly.
I said I'd be happy to help you escape from that house of mannequins and buy you the best toy in Eastside. That wasn't a lie.
I also want to hear the truth from you.
Let's talk about those people you tricked in Eastside.
Oliver glimpses the list you've collected and looks up innocently.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Tricked... What do you mean? I have no idea...
Oliver!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oh, I simply fell in front of them accidentally, showed them my injuries accidentally, and told them I hadn't eaten in days accidentally...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: They all voluntarily helped Oliver. Are you saying that's Oliver's fault too?
Ignoring your warnings, Oliver smirks cunningly, head tilting as if certain you can't catch any solid evidence.
You won't stop lying even now? Your aunt's family is completely under your control, where did those scars on your body come from?
The Bureau's doctor has already examined them. They are all self-inflicted!
You throw out those badges of the Homeless that Oliver used while escaping.
What about these fake badges then? Are they an accident too?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: What are these? Oliver has no idea.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Did you guys pick these up somewhere? Some poor child must have dropped them. You must return them quickly.
Feigning innocence, Oliver pushes the evidence back to you, along with your last bit of patience and sympathy.
...I'm giving you one last chance, Oliver.
I believe not all Sinners are as irredeemable as people say. Many of the Sinners I've encountered simply had no other choices.
You just said you wanted to go home. Why not start by explaining what's going on at home?
If you were treated unfairly or hiding a secret, I'll try my best to help. But first, you have to tell the truth.
You pull out a stack of photos showing the horrific scenes from the basement of that house.
We just saw them not long ago. Don't tell me you don't know what you're looking at.
Why did you do this?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Why... Oh, Oliver wants to know why too...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Why must Oliver eat their leftovers, use their worn-out things, and wear their hand-me-downs...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I tried so hard to please them. No matter what they did, I always smiled. Why did they still scold me, order me around, call my smile fake and disgusting? If they thought I was a burden, they could have just thrown me away!
These grievances are genuine. You can tell these emotions are not a lie.
It's them who mistreated you. You've already told me that, and I believe you.
So you did all this out of revenge?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Revenge? Oliver is a good child. I would never take revenge on them.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oliver promised to get along with them. I must keep my word!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: ...Did you know how easy it is to control the puppets? It's just like playing house. With our shadows cast on the window, we look just like a happy family!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Cousin pours water for me, Auntie cooks for me, and Uncle takes me to school...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Everyone believes it. They think Oliver is a good child! Oliver did it! I'm so smart, aren't I?
Oliver laughs gleefully, hugging the toy and rocking the interrogation chair.
You scrutinize Oliver's face closely, but not even a trace of regret can be found.
You sigh and tidy up the scattered evidence on the table, then stand up and make your way out.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Wait, where are you going? Are you going to leave Oliver alone here?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: What did Oliver do wrong? Why won't you let me go home!
You know full well what you did wrong... There's no need to continue the interrogation.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Huh?
I forgot to tell you that after the toy factory incident, the MBCC investigated everyone involved.
We've found that the transformation is not random. Most people turn into the object they're most familiar with.
If I'm not mistaken, Eve turned you into a toy unicorn, didn't she?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: ...What, what are you bringing this up for?
Nothing... I specifically allowed you to bring the toy into the interrogation room.
I wonder how this toy would feel, having heard what you just said.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: It's all Mommy's fault... I've left you nothing...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: That's not true! This unicorn Mommy gave me is my favorite.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Silly child. What would a toy do for you...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Take this, keep it safe...
A priceless opal necklace was sewn into the heart of the toy.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I don't want it! I don't want this! I just want Mommy to be with me, by my side!

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Shh, don't cry... Mommy can't do that anymore. It'll be with you on my behalf.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: From now on, you have to be a good child on your own. Listen to your aunt and uncle, get along with them, and grow up healthily...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I know my Oliver is the sweetest child...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: That's not true... Oliver hasn't been good...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I haven't been good at all... I'm sorry... Mommy...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: But I have no other choice... Don't go... Wait for me...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Wait, don't go...!
Oliver suddenly grabs you as you're about to get up and leave, tears welling up in those big eyes.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: They made me do it! Auntie and her family gambled all their money away! They wanted to take Mommy's necklace from me, to pay off their debts!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I was obedient until then! I listened to everything they said! I'd thought it all out. I'll be able to leave and support myself once I grow up!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: They went too far! Oliver wanted to be a good child! But I had no choice!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Please don't...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Please don't hate Oliver...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Nightingale! Have you seen Chief today?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief is very busy now. What do you need?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oh, I thought so... I've tried to look for Chief many times but I always get the same answer.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: It's okay. I understand Chief's work is very important...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Can you pass a message to Chief please, Nightingale? Just one sentence!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: What is it?

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oliver has been eating well these past few days! I've also attended the foundation classes arranged by the Bureau!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I've learned a lot of new things! Everyone says Oliver is a fast learner and that I'm bright!

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Oliver doesn't lie anymore... I've also lent a hand to many people...

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: I guess... Oliver has become a good child...
Oliver's head drops lower and lower.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: That's more than one sentence... Forget it. I don't want to leave a message anymore.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: That's not a problem. Also, I happen to need to see you too.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: Is it about... the bad things Oliver did before? You're going to punish me, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: No, Chief has something to give you.

steps.speaker: Oliver
steps.content: ...This is!
If you think you're a good child, I'd be happy to help you escape from here and buy you the best toy in Eastside.
The child runs into the giant colorful toy and starts crying loudly, like a newborn in the most loving embrace in the world.
